alt.en: A coloured print inside a pale blue ornamental frame. At the left a square-rigged sailing ship heels over in rough green water. Across the channel a rocky point carries a lighthouse and a long fortress wall flying flags, and on the right a stone bastion with a domed sentry box rises from the water. Lettering reads "JSLA DE CUBA" (Isla spelled with a J) above the picture and "MORRO Y ENTRADA DEL PUERTO DE LA HABANA" below it.
alt.es: Una estampa en color dentro de un marco ornamental azul claro. A la izquierda, un velero de aparejo de cruz escora en un agua verde y agitada. Al otro lado del canal, una punta rocosa sostiene un faro y una larga muralla de fortaleza con banderas, y a la derecha se alza del agua un baluarte de piedra con una garita de cúpula. Arriba se lee "JSLA DE CUBA" (Isla escrita con J) y abajo "MORRO Y ENTRADA DEL PUERTO DE LA HABANA".

caption.en: El Morro and the mouth of Havana harbour in the Album pintoresco de la isla de Cuba, a book of Cuban views printed in Berlin in the 1850s: the city of the song's first line, "Cuando salí de la Habana".
caption.es: El Morro y la entrada del puerto de La Habana en el Album pintoresco de la isla de Cuba, un libro de vistas cubanas impreso en Berlín en la década de 1850: la ciudad del primer verso de la canción, "Cuando salí de la Habana".

source: "Morro y entrada del puerto de la Habana", plate 1 in Album pintoresco de la isla de Cuba ([Havana?]: B. May, [185-?]; printed in Berlin by Storch & Kramer)
licenceEvidence: Printed in the 1850s (Houghton's own record: "[185-?]"; the Commons page says 1859); no artist named; anyone working on it in the 1850s died long before 1956, so life plus 70 has ended (US: published before 1931). Houghton's statement on the file page: "Houghton Library and Harvard University claim no rights in this photographic reproduction of the work, and the image is free to download and reproduce for any use, commercial or non-commercial"; Commons tag {{PD-art|PD-old-100-1923}} (see rights.md).

alt.en: The top of a printed newspaper page numbered 344, headed "PRIMES 1864 1865 DU MÉNESTREL". Below, in large type, "FLEURS D'ESPAGNE", "25 chansons" and "del maestro YRADIER", over four columns of numbered song titles; number 14 reads "La Paloma (Colombe)". At the foot: "Paroles de MM. Paul Bernard & Tagliafico".
alt.es: La parte de arriba de una página de periódico impresa, con el número 344 y el encabezado "PRIMES 1864 1865 DU MÉNESTREL". Debajo, en letra grande, "FLEURS D'ESPAGNE", "25 chansons" y "del maestro YRADIER", sobre cuatro columnas de títulos numerados; el número 14 dice "La Paloma (Colombe)". Al pie: "Paroles de MM. Paul Bernard & Tagliafico".

caption.en: The Paris weekly Le Ménestrel offers its subscribers 25 Iradier songs with French words for 1864 to 1865, with "La Paloma (Colombe)" as No. 14, five years after the Madrid edition.
caption.es: El semanario parisino Le Ménestrel ofrece a sus suscriptores 25 canciones de Iradier con letra en francés para 1864 a 1865, con "La Paloma (Colombe)" como n.º 14, cinco años después de la edición de Madrid.

source: Le Ménestrel, 31st year (Paris: Heugel, Sunday 25 September 1864), p. 344, "Primes 1864-1865 du Ménestrel", "Fleurs d'Espagne" (top of the page)
library: Boston Public Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Printed Paris 1864; publisher and director J. L. Heugel died 1883; the French words' writers Paul Bernard (died 1879) and D. Tagliafico (died 1900); Iradier died 1865. PD in the US (published before 1931), the EU and Israel (life plus 70 ended by 1971). Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).
credit: Boston Public Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A printed page of music numbered 66, headed "LA PALOMA. (FLY, DOVE, O'ER THE BILLOW.)", with "Translated by L. C. Elson" and "YRADIER". It is marked Allegretto, in 2/4, for voice and piano. Under the voice line, marked CANTO, four lines of words alternate English and Spanish, beginning "The day when I left the land to sail o'er the sea" and "Cuan-do sa-li de la Ha-ba-na Val-ga-me Dios!". At the foot: "Copyright, 1878, by White, Smith & Co."
alt.es: Una página de música impresa con el número 66, encabezada "LA PALOMA. (FLY, DOVE, O'ER THE BILLOW.)", con "Translated by L. C. Elson" e "YRADIER". Lleva la indicación Allegretto, en 2/4, para voz y piano. Bajo la línea de la voz, marcada CANTO, cuatro líneas de letra alternan inglés y español, empezando por "The day when I left the land to sail o'er the sea" y "Cuan-do sa-li de la Ha-ba-na Val-ga-me Dios!". Al pie: "Copyright, 1878, by White, Smith & Co."

caption.en: La Paloma as "Fly, Dove, o'er the Billow" in the Artists' Vocal Album (Boston, 1887), with L. C. Elson's English over the Spanish and its page marked "Copyright, 1878": the print we checked our New York edition against.
caption.es: La Paloma como "Fly, Dove, o'er the Billow" en el Artists' Vocal Album (Boston, 1887), con la letra inglesa de L. C. Elson sobre la española y su página marcada "Copyright, 1878": el impreso con el que cotejamos nuestra edición de Nueva York.

source: Artists' Vocal Album (Boston: White, Smith & Co., 1887), p. 66, "La Paloma (Fly, Dove, o'er the Billow)", translated by L. C. Elson, plate 6521-4
library: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, Music Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: Internet Archive artistsvocalalbu00bost, image n73; UNC record b4916264
licenceEvidence: Printed Boston 1887 (page copyright 1878); English words L. C. Elson died 1920; Iradier died 1865. PD in the US (published before 1931), the EU and Israel (life plus 70 ended 1990). Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).
